Book the First--Recalled to Life




CHAPTER I.
The Period

BOOK-THE-FIRST-I The harbour was grey and the wind came in off the
water in long cold gusts. Nobody on the quay seemed to notice, for
they had all seen worse weather than this. He counted the coins in his
pocket twice and found the sum no larger the second time. There was a
lamp burning in the window of the inn, and he walked towards it
slowly.

Nobody on the quay seemed to notice, for they had all seen worse
weather than this. He counted the coins in his pocket twice and found
the sum no larger the second time. There was a lamp burning in the
window of the inn, and he walked towards it slowly. The landlord
looked up from his ledger, frowned, and then pretended to be busy
again.

He counted the coins in his pocket twice and found the sum no larger
the second time. There was a lamp burning in the window of the inn,
and he walked towards it slowly. The landlord looked up from his
ledger, frowned, and then pretended to be busy again. It was agreed at
last that he should have the small room at the top of the stairs.

There was a lamp burning in the window of the inn, and he walked
towards it slowly. The landlord looked up from his ledger, frowned,
and then pretended to be busy again. It was agreed at last that he
should have the small room at the top of the stairs. All night the
shutters knocked against the wall and he lay awake listening to them.

The landlord looked up from his ledger, frowned, and then pretended to
be busy again. It was agreed at last that he should have the small
room at the top of the stairs. All night the shutters knocked against
the wall and he lay awake listening to them. In the morning the fog
had lifted and the ships stood out sharply against the sky.

CHAPTER III.
A Disappointment

BOOK-THE-SECOND-III It was agreed at last that he should have the

the fog had lifted and the ships stood out sharply against the sky.
The harbour was grey and the wind came in off the water in long cold
gusts.

CHAPTER III.
The Shadow

BOOK-THE-THIRD-III The harbour was grey and the wind came in off the

Nobody on the quay seemed to notice, for they had all seen worse
